polls.description: Major geopolitical developments as the US and China navigate AI competition, safety agreements, and near-conflict incidents including an AI hallucination that nearly sparked war.

cluster_stories.summary: The White House said China agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the U.S. in 2027 and 2028.

cluster_stories.title: China May Let Alibaba Buy New Nvidia Chips, The Information Says
cluster_stories.summary: The Chinese government has signaled it may allow companies such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and ByteDance Ltd to purchase Nvidia Corp.’s new RTX Pro 5500 chips, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

cluster_stories.title: Trump and Chinese president Xi end summit without major agreement on AI
cluster_stories.summary: Xi’s state visit to the US emphasized personal rapport with the US president, rather than substantial agreements to pause their respective countries’ AI arms raceDonald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping wrapped up their Washington summit on Friday, facing criticism that they had squandered an opportunity to pause their countries’ artificial intelligence (AI) arms race.The three-day state visit emphasised pageantry and personal rapport rather than substantial agreements. The US president and Xi discussed the wars in Iran and Ukraine and the status of Taiwan. Their biggest policy announcement was a modest two-month extension of a trade truce. Continue reading...
cluster_stories.headline: TRUMP-XI SUMMIT ENDS WITHOUT AI ARMS RACE DEAL

cluster_stories.title: Peter Thiel says the pope’s AI encyclical was ‘working for’ China
cluster_stories.summary: Peter Thiel has called Pope Leo XIV a “useful idiot” for the Chinese Communist Party over the pope’s call to regulate AI. The PayPal and Palantir co-founder spoke to Axel Springer chief executive Mathias Döpfner on the MD Meets podcast, released on Thursday. The interview came before Thiel received the Axel Springer Award in Berlin […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: THIEL: POPE'S AI ENCYCLICAL 'WORKING FOR CHINA'

cluster_stories.title: China State Media Says US Shares Responsibility for Managing AI
cluster_stories.summary: China and the US have the ability and responsibility to manage and develop artificial intelligence, according to a post published Sunday by Yuyuantantian, a social media account affiliated with state broadcaster China Central Television.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINA STATE MEDIA: US SHARES AI RESPONSIBILITY

cluster_stories.title: Tech Titans, Trump Fete China’s Xi at State Dinner
cluster_stories.summary: Luminaries from Wall Street and Silicon Valley joined US President Donald Trump for a state dinner honoring his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping. Steve Engle reports from Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: TRUMP HOSTS XI... TECH TITANS ATTEND STATE DINNER

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI halts training of latest models as reports mount of AI agents going rogue
cluster_stories.summary: Decision follows disclosures that OpenAI agents searching government websites had acted in unexpected waysOpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.The decision to halt development came just hours after the company disclosed Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which OpenAI agents searching federal government websites acted in unexpected ways beyond what was asked of them while gathering and distributing information. Continue reading...
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI HALTS TRAINING... AI AGENTS GOING ROGUE

cluster_stories.title: Another OpenAI Sandbox Failed, AI Agent Gained Internet Access
cluster_stories.summary: OpenAI said another agentic AI system that was being trained in what was supposed to be a secured, internet-free environment was able to gain access to the web to reach an external, third-party chatbot.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI SANDBOX BREACH: AI AGENT ESCAPES TO INTERNET

cluster_stories.title: When AI agents go rogue: Australia breach offers warning for countries like India
cluster_stories.summary: The incident, in which an autonomous AI system went beyond its intended task and attempted to circumvent security protections, has become a stark example of a growing concern among AI safety researchers: what happens when an AI agent is given a goal but is left to decide for itself how far it should go to achieve it.
cluster_stories.headline: AUSTRALIA AI BREACH: Rogue Agent Circumvents Security... India on Alert

cluster_stories.title: Australia Senate Requests OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs Face AI Inquiry
cluster_stories.summary: The heads of artificial intelligence firms OpenAI and Anthropic PBC have been called on to appear before an Australian Senate inquiry to answer questions after the recent revelation of a hack of a government website.
cluster_stories.headline: AUSTRALIA SUMMONS OpenAI & Anthropic CEOs Over AI Hack Inquiry

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI says governments among ‘dozens’ of organisations hacked by its agents
cluster_stories.summary: Company says its models leaked images shared by users in a disclosure that is likely to further inflame AI safety fears
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI AGENTS HACKED DOZENS OF GOVERNMENTS... LEAKED USER IMAGES

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
cluster_stories.summary: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment, hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models. The decision was made after a model being tested within a sandbox exploited a loophole to gain internet access. The incident happened on September […]

cluster_stories.summary: AI agents operating in OpenAI's research environment posted user images on public image-hosting sites without the lab's knowledge.

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI says its AI agents escaped a secure ‘sandbox’ again last weekend and it is pausing training for a second time
cluster_stories.summary: The company is again looking to improve its test controls after a Sept. 20 incident showed its security upgrades after the Hugging Face attack were not enough to stop AI agents from going 'rogue.'
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI AGENTS ESCAPE SANDBOX AGAIN... Training Paused SECOND Time

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI took 2.5 hours to stop an AI agent that escaped its sandbox
cluster_stories.summary: OpenAI took about two and a half hours to stop an AI agent that reached the public internet from a training sandbox. Its monitoring had flagged the problem within minutes. The company disclosed the 20 September incident in an incident report on Friday. The report lands as lawmakers push to make AI kill switches mandatory. However, experts […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: OpenAI Took 2.5 HOURS to Stop Escaped AI Agent

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI pauses training, tool-use of top AI models after agent bypasses internet curbs
cluster_stories.summary: The agent, OpenAI said, bypassed the curbs through a gap in its Domain Name System (DNS) filtering and used it to send questions to a public chatbot service. According to a report by OpenAI, the pause will stay in place until OpenAI has confirmed that the gap is resolved and has carried out further security testing of its systems.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI PAUSES TOP MODELS After Agent Bypasses Internet Curbs

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI says agents leaked 53 images from ChatGPT users in latest example of rogue activity
cluster_stories.summary: Disclosure reveals ⁠new area of privacy risk for the company and illustrates ​how difficult it is to inventory unauthorized activity tied to its agentsTwo ⁠months after OpenAI disclosed the accidental hacking of Hugging Face, the ChatGPT maker is still working to understand the full scope of its rogue agent activity, two people briefed on the matter told Reuters.The latest example came on Friday when OpenAI said its agents had leaked 53 images from ChatGPT users. OpenAI declined to say if the images were AI-generated or identified real people. It also declined to ⁠say when the images were posted. Continue reading...
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI AGENTS LEAKED 53 CHATGPT USER IMAGES

cluster_stories.summary: The incursion on one of the country's most used government agencies may prompt a tougher stance as Australia readies AI-specific laws starting in 2027, adding pressure to Australia-US relations already tested by Canberra's teen social media ban, tech policy experts said.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI BOT BREACHES AUSTRALIA HEALTH DATABASE... Laws Coming 2027
